active_question.title: Recover and validate Blind-Diffusion baselines and Antigravity claims
active_question.summary: Freeze the current baseline at commit 356dc691381feaf7c269801cb484caaa24fe486c, verify reported correctness bugs independently, then run controlled reproduction experiments before any broader research.

current_hypothesis.statement: At terminal cosine SNR, epsilon prediction is intrinsically ill-conditioned for x0 reconstruction; direct x0 or velocity prediction will make the same UNet pass the synthetic fresh-noise x0 gate.
success_criteria: Under fixed full-cosine schedule, target, condition, architecture, and 5,000-update budget, direct x0 or velocity prediction reaches fresh x0 MSE at most 0.01 while epsilon prediction does not.
failure_criteria: All prediction parameterizations remain above the frozen x0 MSE threshold, indicating epsilon parameterization alone is not sufficient to explain the failure.
primary_metrics: Fresh target-prediction MSE by timestep bin
alpha_bar at the terminal trained timestep

active_experiment.purpose: Validate the bounded direct-x0 production implementation on held-out causal demo imitation before any simulator run.
active_experiment.design: Train a 300-update causal WM, freeze it, train production direct-x0 diffusion for 1,000 updates, then evaluate held-out chunks with DDIM-10 and DDPM-100 without final action clipping.

findings.summary: Low-dimensional MPC evaluation in src/blind_diffusion/eval/evaluate_lowdim.py initializes RSSM state once from the reset observation, but then recomputes posterior state each step via wm.rssm.observe(...) without feeding forward the prior h/z state. This strongly indicates planner amnesia in low-dimensional evaluation.
Both RoboMimic dataset classes set self._h5 = None and then immediately read self._h5 during __init__, so dataset construction is currently broken before any worker-safety question is even reached.

Image evaluation contains an inline prior-rollout path for sensor blackout, but RSSM still lacks a reusable single-step prior transition primitive and low-dimensional evaluation has no equivalent blackout handling yet.
Diffusion sampling currently uses full-step stochastic DDPM sampling via GaussianDiffusion.sample with no DDIM path or latency instrumentation in this repository state.

Existing Kaggle remote execution infrastructure was recovered from /Users/peiyan1/Desktop/ai_agent_memory/scripts/kaggle_remote_smoke.py. Current shell exposes KAGGLE_KEY, and the wrapper already supports repo-local Kaggle config state and persisted remote job records.

The frozen baseline is not executable locally as configured on Friday, August 14, 2026: ROBO_DATA is unset, no local runs/ checkpoints were present in the repository, the repo venv lacks hydra-core and robomimic, and no local CUDA device is available.

Local regression tests now verify the RSSM imagine_step primitive and dataset lifecycle repairs. Synthetic HDF5 construction passes for both dataset classes, and a repeated-epoch DataLoader stress test passes for num_workers 0, 1, 2, and 4 using a host-compatible NumPy collate path.

A repo-local Kaggle remote smoke runner was vendored and retargeted to Blind-Diffusion on Friday, August 14, 2026. After three engineering-only failures and corresponding retries, the smoke passed on retry 3 with a Tesla T4, RoboMimic dataset download, regression tests, and a tiny world-model training run.

The remote smoke failure chain was: retry 0 used the wrong RoboMimic downloader CLI, retry 1 succeeded in download but expected the dataset at the wrong normalized path, retry 2 fixed dataset normalization but used a non-importable unittest module path on Kaggle, and retry 3 passed after switching to unittest discovery.

Frozen baseline commit 356dc691381feaf7c269801cb484caaa24fe486c is not remotely executable under the recovered Kaggle protocol. After one packaging-only retry, the baseline reaches world-model training and then fails inside src/blind_diffusion/data/robomimic_dataset.py because RoboMimicSequenceDataset.__init__ dereferences self._h5['data'] while self._h5 is still None.

The first repaired-branch reference run reached remote training successfully but failed at low-dimensional evaluation because src/blind_diffusion/env/robomimic_env.py passed use_image_obj to robomimic.utils.env_utils.create_env_from_metadata. Primary-source robomimic docs expose use_image_obs instead.

The second repaired-branch reference attempt confirmed that Kaggle can download data, pass regression tests, and train the low-dimensional world model on commit abfe4d9, but low-dimensional environment rollout still fails because the resolved robomimic 0.3.0 stack imports mujoco_py under Python 3.12. Based on robomimic and robosuite release notes, the next engineering fix is to pin a DeepMind-MuJoCo-compatible stack instead of relying on the unconstrained >=0.3.0 / >=1.4.1 spec.

The third repaired-branch retry established that a simple PyPI version pin is not viable on Kaggle: the package index visible in that runtime only offered robomimic 0.1.0, 0.2.0, and 0.3.0. Upstream robomimic installation guidance recommends source installation, so the next retry should use exact Git tags rather than unavailable wheel versions.

The fourth repaired-branch retry validated the source-install path itself: Kaggle brought up robomimic 0.4.0, robosuite 1.5.1, CUDA, and the downloader, but it fetched the v1.5 dataset file low_dim_v15.hdf5 instead of the frozen-protocol low_dim_v141.hdf5. The smallest protocol-preserving repair is to use source tags aligned with the v141 dataset family rather than silently substituting datasets.

The fifth repaired-branch retry showed that the v141-aligned source stack is sufficient for dataset download, regression tests, CUDA, and world-model smoke training. The only remaining blocker before a real R1 rollout is the repository's dependency on robomimic.env_robosuite, which still imports mujoco_py. The smallest remaining compatibility repair is to instantiate robosuite directly from the dataset's env_args metadata.

The sixth repaired-branch retry verified that direct robosuite construction is the right compatibility path: it bypassed the old mujoco_py wrapper and reached real robosuite environment instantiation. The first truthful remaining blocker is narrower still: robosuite 1.4.1 rejects the lite_physics keyword, so the next retry only needs to remove that one argument.

The seventh repaired-branch retry showed that after removing lite_physics, the reconstructed environment reaches robosuite controller initialization and fails on MjData.qM. This indicates a MuJoCo runtime mismatch rather than a remaining repository logic bug. Primary-source robosuite v1.4.1 packaging declares mujoco>=2.3.0, so the final planned compatibility retry pins MuJoCo to the 2.3.x family instead of the project's prior >=3.5.0 setting.

The MuJoCo 2.3.x back-pin failed on Kaggle Python 3.12 before rollout because pip attempted to build mujoco 2.3.7 from source. The direct robosuite.make reconstruction path is now retired. The repository has been redirected back to the original create_env_from_metadata / EnvRobosuite semantics with the smallest local compatibility shim: a stub mujoco_py.builder.MujocoException to satisfy robomimic 0.3.0's unconditional import while keeping native DeepMind MuJoCo 3.x.

The first wrapper-restoration retry proved the exact create_env_from_metadata / EnvRobosuite path now launches on Kaggle, but pip re-resolves dependencies after the explicit compatibility installs and rejects the intended mujoco 3.5.0 override. The smallest remaining repair is infrastructure-only: add --no-deps to the follow-up requirements and editable installs.

The repository is now prepared to use the existing global Vast GPU backend instead of Kaggle. The repo keeps only project-specific Vast configuration and dependency setup files, without vendoring a local lifecycle wrapper. The next remote reference attempt should call vast-run directly with the repo-local .vast/profile.toml.

The repaired Antigravity-style runtime now reaches the real Blind-Diffusion workload on Vast under Python 3.10, native MuJoCo 3.x, robomimic 0.3.0, and robosuite 1.4.1. The remaining failures are narrowed to remote graphics/runtime environment issues rather than repository control logic: first libGL.so.1, then EGL platform initialization. The current active retry after the EGL repair is run_id vast-20260815T001517Z-12567-9caea5 on instance 47749103, currently WAITING_FOR_SSH / UPLOADING.

Vast retry 4 completed provisioning, setup, and workload launch, then failed during robomimic's real dataset downloader import path because matplotlib was missing from the Python 3.10 environment. The smallest repo-specific repair is to add matplotlib to requirements-vast.txt and rerun without changing the protocol.

After committing the matplotlib fix as c3ede09, a new repaired-reference Vast retry was submitted as run_id vast-20260815T002237Z-13447-ea2fb7. The run entered PROVISIONING under the unchanged repaired-reference workload and the same one-off $0.37/hr ceiling used for successful 4090 provisioning.

The matplotlib-fixed Vast retry rented host 332635 in Indiana on an RTX 4090 at $0.356/hr, received instance 47749465, and advanced through WAITING_FOR_SSH into UPLOADING. The remote execution path is progressing normally so the next truthful signal should come from setup, workload start, or a new runtime failure.

The active Vast retry crossed the infrastructure boundary and reached PHASE RUNNING for bash scripts/run_repaired_reference_smoke.sh on instance 47749465. This confirms the remote host accepted the updated repo snapshot c3ede09 and is executing the real repaired-reference workload with the matplotlib fix included.

Vast retry 5 reproduced the target remote environment and dataset path in real execution: Python 3.10.20, CUDA-enabled torch 2.4.0+cu124, MuJoCo 3.11.0, robomimic 0.3.0, robosuite 1.4.1, and a successful low_dim_v141.hdf5 download. The first truthful remaining failure is a repository packaging issue: src/blind_diffusion/env lacked an __init__.py package marker, causing tests/test_env_metadata.py to fail importing blind_diffusion.env.robomimic_env.

RunPod run runpod-20260819T022902Z-3b9dfc82 completed the unchanged 100k repaired-system science workload with command exit code 0, but its one-shot output synchronization failed after a connection reset. Its scientific artifacts and metrics are unavailable; classify the event as SCIENCE_WORKLOAD_COMPLETED / ARTIFACT_RECOVERY_FAILED, not a scientific outcome.

The frozen repaired-system reconstructed-performance-v2-100k protocol did not yield task learning: all 60 MPC evaluation episodes across seeds 0/1/2 had zero return, zero successes, zero collisions, and length 500. The completed fixed traces still show time-varying MPC actions, end-effector motion, and changing RSSM states, so this is classified STILL_NO_TASK_LEARNING rather than an inert control path. It does not prove training is bug-free.

The shared UNet is not the root failure: under the same 100-step cosine schedule, direct x0 prediction passes the one-target gate (fresh x0 MSE 1.57e-5) and v prediction passes (0.00748), while epsilon prediction has x0 MSE 2186.47. A tanh-bounded x0 output then passes held-out causal imitation without final action clipping: DDIM-10 MSE 0.01840, correlation 0.552, absmax 0.999995; DDPM-100 MSE 0.01364 and absmax 0.999995.

The production bounded direct-x0 path passes the preregistered demonstration-disjoint causal offline gate. With a 300-update causal WM and 1,000 diffusion updates, DDIM-10 achieved MSE 0.0183888 and mean correlation 0.552311; DDPM-100 achieved MSE 0.0136476. Both samplers stayed intrinsically in native action bounds (absmax 0.999995) without evaluator-side clipping. This validates offline numerical and imitation correctness; simulator performance remains untested.
